purpose: Taxonomy for evaluating cultural language source categories as inputs to the FusionCanvas Phrase Intelligence Database.

categories.notes: Durable cultural language with strong recognition and many public-domain or traditional sources; still track variants and provenance.
Common idioms are useful for literalization and niche twists; review source licenses and avoid copying proprietary definitions or examples.
Often culturally powerful and structurally reusable, but exact phrases can be associated with people, shows, brands, or campaigns.
Valuable for catchphrase mechanics, cadence, and reference detection; do not treat exact quotes as product-ready text.
Useful for recurring line structures, character voice, and cultural reference detection; prefer abstract templates and metadata.
Some quotes are public domain or widely traditional, while others are modern, misattributed, or rights-sensitive; review attribution and use context.
Titles can be short, rhythmic, and adaptable, but many are strongly associated with artists or recordings; use careful review and transformation.
Lyrics are valuable for cadence, repetition, and emotional compression, but exact text should not be used directly in products.
Designed to be memorable and persuasive, making them excellent structural inputs but poor direct-use candidates.
Highly current source of caption formats, joke structures, and snowclones; exact meme text may involve creators, platforms, copyrighted media, or brands.
Core phrase-family assets with explicit slots; review the origin phrase and store generic templates when direct phrase text is sensitive.
Useful for title mechanics, curiosity gaps, contrast, and topical phrasing; avoid copying full proprietary headlines as product text.
Good source for list formats, how-to structures, and niche language; exact titles require source and originality review.
Captures authentic community phrasing and recurring rhetorical moves; protect privacy and avoid importing identifiable user content verbatim.
Strong signal for current community phrasing, jokes, and templates; use platform-compliant access, privacy controls, and abstraction where possible.
Excellent for attention structures, escalation, challenges, and title formulas; avoid copying distinctive creator titles directly.
Useful for conversational formats, episode-title patterns, and niche identity language; review show names and creator-specific phrasing.
Often identifies fast-moving cultural patterns; exact wording may be creator-associated, platform-specific, or trend-sensitive.
Good source for durable phrasing, rhetorical structures, and quotation patterns when public-domain status and source edition are clear.
Packaging, signs, listings, and marketing copy reveal persuasive mechanics and category conventions, but exact language is usually unsuitable for reuse.
Common workplace phrases are useful for identity, boundary, and faux-authority templates; review modern slogans or employer-specific phrases.
